description: Fix the monster duplication bug when feeding (and any other care action). ROOT CAUSE confirmed via live Playwright reproduction: in packages/frontend/src/App.tsx, two sibling children of .sprite-wrap share the same React key when a care FX is active - the bounce-layer div uses key={careFx?.key ?? "idle"} and the care-fx <span> uses key={careFx.key}. When careFx is {action, key:N} both siblings get key N. React keys must be unique among siblings; the collision corrupts reconciliation so when careFx reverts to null the previous bounce-layer div is left un-unmounted, producing TWO .sprite-bounce-layer divs / two sprite SVGs that persist = the duplicated monster. A single Feed click reproduces it. Fix is frontend-only (no backend/infra change, no redeploy of backend logic). This repo is set up on branch main; create the feature branch as the first step.
steps: From the repo root (/projects/sandbox/kiro-digitalmonster), ensure you are on a clean main, then create and switch to a feature branch: `git checkout -b fix/feed-monster-duplication`. Do NOT push. Do NOT touch backup/previous-main.

Run `npm install` at the repo root if node_modules is missing, then establish the baseline: `npm run build` succeeds, `npm test` (root/shared) is green, and `cd packages/frontend && npm test` is green (50 tests). Record the baseline counts.

In packages/frontend/src/App.tsx, change the bounce-layer div's key so it can NEVER equal the numeric careFx.key used by the sibling care-fx <span>. Replace `key={careFx?.key ?? "idle"}` with a string-namespaced key, e.g. `key={careFx === null ? "idle" : `fx-${careFx.key}`}`. Leave the care-fx <span>'s own key as careFx.key (now in a different value space from the div). Do NOT change the className logic, the MonsterSprite child, the SpeechBubble, or the zzz/dirt overlays.

Verify the sibling keys inside .sprite-wrap are now all distinct in every render state (idle: bounce-layer key "idle", no care-fx span; active: bounce-layer key "fx-N", care-fx span key N). Confirm the keyed remount that re-fires the bounce animation on repeated same-action clicks is preserved (the key still changes each action because careFx.key increments).
Re-run `npm run build` (root), `npm test` (root/shared), and `cd packages/frontend && npm test` to confirm all remain green and the TypeScript build still passes.

Build and serve the frontend locally (or use `npm run dev` in packages/frontend) and use the Playwright power to click the Feed (餌やり) button once and then several times rapidly; after animations settle, assert via document.querySelectorAll('.sprite-wrap svg').length === 1 and document.querySelectorAll('.sprite-bounce-layer').length === 1. Also confirm the 🍖 feed emoji FX and the SpeechBubble still appear. Save a screenshot of the single-monster result to .agents/tasks/task-fix-feed-duplication/ or the Playwright artifacts dir and note the path in findings. If a local server cannot be stood up in the sandbox, document that and rely on build + the DOM-key reasoning; note it in findings.

Commit the change on the feature branch with a clear message, e.g. `fix(frontend): prevent monster duplication by removing sibling React key collision in sprite FX layer`. Keep the commit limited to App.tsx (plus package-lock.json only if npm install legitimately changed it - prefer not staging unrelated lockfile churn).
acceptance_criteria: After clicking Feed once and after clicking it repeatedly, exactly ONE sprite SVG and ONE .sprite-bounce-layer remain inside .sprite-wrap (no leftover/orphaned layer).
The feed effect still works: hunger reduces, a little HP restores, the 🍖 feed FX plays (issue #10 behavior preserved) and the SpeechBubble (issue #11) still renders.
The bounce animation still re-fires when the SAME care action is clicked repeatedly (keyed remount preserved).
`npm run build` at the repo root succeeds.
`npm test` at the repo root (shared) stays green at baseline; `cd packages/frontend && npm test` stays green at baseline (50).
No new runtime dependencies added; JA text and i18n unchanged; only frontend files changed (no backend/infra).
verification: npm test (repo root) all shared tests pass
cd packages/frontend && npm test all pass (50)
Playwright/manual: feed the monster; confirm document.querySelectorAll('.sprite-wrap svg').length === 1 and document.querySelectorAll('.sprite-bounce-layer').length === 1 after the FX settles
findings:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED and FIXED. In packages/frontend/src/App.tsx, inside .sprite-wrap, the bounce-layer div used key={careFx?.key ?? "idle"} and the sibling care-fx <span> used key={careFx.key}. When a care FX was active (e.g. careFx={action:'feed', key:1}) BOTH siblings got the numeric key 1, violating React's unique-sibling-key rule and corrupting reconciliation; when careFx reverted to null the old bounce-layer node was not unmounted, leaving two .sprite-bounce-layer divs / two sprite SVGs = the duplicated monster.

FIX (frontend-only, single line): changed the bounce-layer div key to a string-namespaced value that can never equal the numeric careFx.key: key={careFx === null ? "idle" : `fx-${careFx.key}`}. The care-fx <span> key stays careFx.key (now in a separate value space). The key still changes every action (careFx.key increments in triggerCareFx), so the keyed remount that re-fires the bounce animation on repeated same-action clicks is preserved. No className changes, no MonsterSprite/SpeechBubble/zzz/dirt changes, no feed-animation (#10) changes, no i18n changes.

FILES CHANGED: packages/frontend/src/App.tsx (one line, the bounce-layer div key). package-lock.json had pre-existing unrelated churn and was intentionally NOT staged.

VERIFICATION: Environment note - npm is not on the default PATH in the sandbox; it lives at /root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin (exported PATH for all npm invocations). 
- Baseline (pre-fix): npm run build (root) exit 0; npm test (root/shared) 47/47 pass; cd packages/frontend && npm test 50/50 pass.
- Post-fix: npm run build (root) exit 0; npm test (root/shared) 47/47 pass; cd packages/frontend && npm test 50/50 pass.
- Live DOM verification via agent-browser against vite dev server (http://localhost:5173): initial {svgs:1, layers:1}; after clicking 餌やり (🍖餌やり) once {svgs:1, layers:1} both during FX and after it settled (careFx:0); after 5 rapid feed clicks and settle {svgs:1, layers:1, careFx:0}. Speech bubble element present. Screenshot of the single-monster result saved to /projects/sandbox/.kiro/artifacts/screenshots/feed-single-monster.png (confirms exactly one sprite). The 'document.querySelectorAll(.sprite-wrap svg).length === 1' and '.sprite-bounce-layer.length === 1' acceptance checks hold after FX settles.

All acceptance criteria met.
